claims: first application submission succeeds and a duplicate returns already_applied
administrator accept and decline both remove the pending row from the current queue
accepted and declined application history still prevents a later re-application
three wrong submissions per independent actor each return wrong_password without a lockout
the correct password creates membership and a repeated correct submission returns already_member
run-owned memberships and site policy are cleaned up after the observation
a run-owned internal invitation can be created and subsequently joined
no credential or opaque token value is persisted by the evidence artifact
the run-owned invited membership is absent after cleanup

password: Wikidot compares the submitted password directly with the configured membership password.
Wrong submissions return wrong_password; the action contains no password-failure counter or lockout threshold.
A successful password join creates membership and removes any application or internal invitation for that actor.
application: An existing application makes a later submission return already_applied.
Administrator accept or decline changes the application status instead of deleting its history row.
Accepted membership is created by the reviewing administrator.
email_invitation: The invitation is selected by opaque hash plus accepted=false; acceptance is not bound to the invitation email address or recipient identity.
There is no invitation-expiry check in the module or acceptance action.
Acceptance marks the invitation accepted and therefore makes the hash one-use.
Administrator cancellation deletes the invitation row, causing the same unavailable module state as an unknown or already-used hash.
Resend reuses the same hash and only limits reminder attempts; it does not rotate the invitation token.
